chunks: Ubaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked
about a man: is it proper for him to sleep while he is junub? He said: “That is disliked until he performs wudu (ablution).”

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in a state of janabah, major ritual impurity
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: it is disliked; legally discouraged but not forbidden

ai.seo_question: Is it disliked to sleep while in a state of janabah without performing wudu?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one in a state of janabah (major ritual impurity). It indicates that sleeping in that state is makruh unless one first performs wudu (ablution).

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.179 - Ubaydullah ibn Ali Al-Halabi said:

‘Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked whether it is appropriate for a man to sleep while in a state of janabah (ritual impurity from sexual discharge).’
Imam (as) replied: 'It is disliked (makruh) to do so without first performing wudu (ablution).'
